title: A very short Thursday post about Spurs, a Hedgehog and a very near miss.
author: Martin Skelton
summary: Martin Skelton uses Tottenham Hotspur's near-relegation in 2025-26 as a parable for school leadership. He argues that for a Premier League club the Hedgehog Concept, in Jim Collins's sense, is obviously winning, since income, brand and recruitment all flow from it. Spurs' own post-season review admitted that football success had not been driving the club's decisions, and the result was repeated failures, poor decisions and a lack of leadership over a sustained period. Skelton then maps this directly onto schools: learning is the school's version of winning, and when it stops driving decisions the school loses confidence, reputation and the ability to see what is happening. His closing move is to ask readers whether their own school needs a reset or is genuinely moving in its chosen direction.
points: The argument rests on one organizing idea: an institution's single core purpose (winning for a club, learning for a school) must be the test applied to every decision.
Spurs' failure is presented as a leadership and decision-making failure, not one bad result, which is why Skelton thinks capable, commercially successful people can still drift.
Skelton lists the consequences of schools drifting from learning: students learn less, stakeholders lose confidence, enrolment falls, staff find the school harder, and people stop noticing.
The practical prompt is a self-audit: ask whether a reset is needed rather than assuming all is well.
quotes: The club ordered a root and branch review, even before the season had ended. The results were published earlier this week.
Even as I write this, it seems obvious to me what the Hedgehog Concept of a Premier league team should be. It’s winning, isn’t it?
This season, which finished a week or so ago, went wrong for Spurs. It very nearly went terribly wrong. Spurs avoided relegation on the very last day of the season.
The Board of Tottenham Hotspur are not idiots. All of them, in their own way have been commercially successful. They have hired staff who are not idiots.

Spurs fall from grace is what happens when we are not clear about our Hedgehog Concept or when we take it for granted and simply assume that it will be all ok. Perhaps Spurs thought that they could ignore ‘winning ‘ for a year while they focused on other things.

So it is for schools and classrooms. Learning is our version of winning. When learning stops ‘driving our decisions’, when this goes on for more ‘than one season alone’, when we have ‘repeated failures’ and ‘make poor decisions’, when we have a ‘lack of leadership’ this is what happens. We get found out.

When we get found out, some of the same things happen in our schools as happened with Spurs. Our children and students fail to learn as well as they could and deserve; our stakeholders lose confidence in us; fewer people want to send their children to us; children and students lose confidence in the place that is, theoretically, supposed to be helping them; the school becomes a harder place in which to work; we lose confidence in the leadership; after a while, we stop seeing what is happening.
